name: Ofir Cohen
headline: Public policy advisor on innovation and technology
shortBio: MPA candidate at Princeton University focusing on AI policy, innovation and economic competitiveness. Former advisor to the U.S. House of Representatives and head of strategy at DNAidea.
fullBio: Ofir Cohen is an MPA candidate at Princeton University with a focus on technology policy, AI, innovation and economic competitiveness. Previously served as an advisor to the U.S. House of Representatives on foreign affairs and economics, and as head of strategy at DNAidea. Works at the intersection of public policy, multi-sector partnerships and innovation, particularly interested in building bridges between government, philanthropy and the private sector around emerging technologies.
highlights: Served as advisor to the U.S. House of Representatives on foreign affairs and economics
Led strategic multi-sector work as head of strategy at DNAidea
Focuses on technology policy, AI and innovation in the public sector

name: Uri Angel
shortBio: Master's student in Energy Systems at Oxford with background in environmental entrepreneurship, energy economics, climate policy and critical minerals.

name: Aaron Simpson-Grossman
role: Legal Officer, IDF and Wharton MBA Candidate
headline: Attorney and officer with experience in security and international affairs
shortBio: Served five years as an officer and attorney in the Military Prosecutor's Office, and contributed to shaping Israel's legal strategy in international arena.
fullBio: Aaron Simpson-Grossman served five years as an officer and attorney in the Military Prosecutor's Office, contributing to Israel's legal strategy in the international arena. He holds degrees in law, economics and finance, and is starting an MBA at Wharton. His interests include investments, dual-use technologies and infrastructure.
highlights: Served as officer and attorney in Military Prosecutor's Office for five years
Contributed to shaping Israel's legal strategy in the international arena
Background in law, economics and finance

name: Uzi Kalchaim

fullBio: Uzi Kalchaim is an attorney and economist with background in public service, economic policy consulting and investments. Previously served as advisor to Ministers of Finance and Defense, and worked in venture capital and private equity. Currently works at Meta Israel as Client Solutions Manager in the Media & Aggregators team.

name: Maya Shiloni
role: Student, Government and Economics, Harvard University
headline: Focused on public policy, intelligence and student leadership
shortBio: Harvard University student in Government and Economics and graduate of Unit 8200. Gained experience in intelligence, product management and public service in the U.S. and Israel.
fullBio: Maya Shiloni is a student at Harvard University in Government and Economics and a graduate of Unit 8200, where she served in project and product management. She gained experience in the public and parliamentary sectors, including an internship with Congressman Josh Gottheimer and work at the Israeli Knesset. She also led significant student initiatives including Harvard College Israel Trek and the International Israel Summit. Her interests include law, public policy and Israeli politics.
highlights: Unit 8200 graduate with experience in intelligence and product management
Gained experience in public and parliamentary sectors in the U.S. and Israel
Led major student initiatives at Harvard and in the Israeli community

name: Omri Attar
role: Former Chief of Staff, Ministry of Diaspora Affairs | Global COO, ELNET

fullBio: Omri Attar is a senior manager and public figure with extensive experience in government service, the global Jewish community and promoting Israel-diaspora relations. He served as chief of staff in the Ministry of Diaspora Affairs and as Global COO of ELNET, working at the intersection of strategy, public policy, community leadership and public diplomacy.

fullBio: Sagie Sharon works at the intersection of education, technology and entrepreneurship, focused on how public systems and educational institutions adapt to a changing technological era.
